answer: Each identity claims one terrace plot and locks a 70-credit bond. A terrace auditor counts vine stems at sowing and harvest and recomputes the growth delta from a table keyed by plot area and sowing date; a delta outside tolerance burns the bond. The first survey costs 29 credits, the k-th fake 29+7(k-1): the 1000th pays 7022, and 1000 fakes pay 3,525,500 plus 70,000 locked, each plot needing its tag and survey. A rented-plot ring fails: rented vine plots carry the seller key tag, matched against the claimant key. An honest identity pays one survey and recovers its bond after a clean audit.
